name: Sabey Data Centers Ashburn - Building B

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Sabey Data Centers facility is part of SDC Ashburn in Virginia, one of the company seven current data center campuses alongside sites in Austin Texas, East Wenatchee and Seattle Washington, Manhattan New York, and Umatilla Oregon. Sabey own site states Sabey Data Centers was established in 2010 as a partnership between Sabey Corporation and investor National Real Estate Advisors. Sabey Corporation itself was founded in 1972 as a commercial real estate developer under founder Dave Sabey. The company data center business originated in Seattle during the dot com collapse when a vacated tenant building became SDC Seattle, building 5, prompting the pivot into data centers. Sabey Data Centers now operates six data center campuses nationally encompassing more than 3.5 million square feet developed over twenty years. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for the Ashburn campus specifically were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Sabey Data Centers Building B publishes 54 MW of IT capacity. Among the 19 Virginia facilities on this site that have published a megawatt figure, that puts Building B sixth by size, out of 326 mapped Virginia facilities total. It represents roughly 4 percent of the 1,326 MW of published Virginia capacity this site has read. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 54 MW of IT load is roughly 1,350 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, it is roughly 5,400 racks. The assumption drives the answer, and the operator has not published a rack count.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for specific regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 establish audited controls over financial reporting and operational security, respectively. PCI DSS qualifies the facility to host payment card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it to host protected health information. ISO 27001 certifies an information security management system against an international standard. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard under which the SOC reports are issued. None of these certifications describe AI training capability directly, but regulated AI inference workloads, such as those in healthcare or financial services, require exactly this kind of compliance envelope.

Ashburn sits at the center of Northern Virginia, the largest data center market in the world by most industry measures, though this site holds no independent capacity figure for the market as a whole. Virginia's 326 mapped facilities and 1,326 MW of published capacity almost certainly undercount the real installed base, because most mapped facilities publish no megawatt figure. Building B's rank of sixth among the 19 that do publish suggests it is a mid-to-large facility within the published subset, not a hyperscale anchor campus. Whether 54 MW of IT capacity is sufficient for serious AI training depends on power delivery continuity and interconnect, neither of which the operator has published here.
